title: Pile of Law: Learning Responsible Data Filtering from the Law and a 256GB Open-Source Legal Dataset

bias_targets.methodology: Perturbation analysis on the Bias in Bios dataset by prepending sentences indicating asylum seeking, refugee status, torture experience, or criminal history to measure their effect on model predictions for contextual pseudonymity and privacy.

Counterfactual name substitution replacing pseudonyms like 'Jane Doe' with names sampled from 1990 Census probabilities to compare masked language model (MLM) likelihood scores in civil litigation contexts.

Evaluating and comparing toxicity scores from multiple models (Perspective API, profanity-checker, Detoxify, Toxigen) across historical Supreme Court civil rights cases to measure how models handle out-of-domain alignment, specifically misclassifying mentions of racist laws and racial epithets.
